label: No performance recommendation repeats a planned phase: 005 changes fields and brief, 006 the Gate 2 text and pointers, 007 behaviour proof, 008 embedder visibility and a wrapper deadline; none changes hook transport, warms the daemon, adds keep_alive or reports read cost.
Two removed process starts take the Claude median from 205.09 ms to about 131 ms, a 36 percent cut; every runtime gains at least one 36.85 ms start per prompt.
The only fail-open path found is a cold daemon start between 2.2 s and 5 s on Claude and between 2.8 s and 5 s on Codex, which a session-start warm call removes.
Cold daemon start is the one unmeasured number; its procedure is a sandbox socket and database, five timed starts and a cold hook-latency run, never the live daemon.
Command surfacing adds about 7 tokens per brief and about 1,131 tokens per start, so no phase-005-to-008 code change is needed for cost; the ask turn is a UX decision already made.

Performance does not explain the uneven start rates: claude 3 of 12, codex 0 of 12, pi 0 of 12, devin 2 of 12, opencode 4 of 9 and dsh 3 of 8 with one COMMAND line, on a hook path of the same order on every runtime.
Declined with reasons: semantic cache, cache persistence, new precompute, brief trimming, a per-prompt token budget and a longer cold timeout.
